title: When the Playlist Falls
premise: In the fading mill town of Harrow Bend, senior class president Beatrix Galloway has spent three years perfecting the art of staying invisible at home while winning every debate on stage. When her best friend Theo vanishes, leaving only his car keys and a half-deleted playlist of songs tied to the town's founding tradition, the Harvest Court, she discovers he was investigating how the town's beloved pageant became a machine for the powerful Delacroix family to decide who belongs in Harrow Bend and who gets quietly erased. As Beatrix rebuilds Theo's trail through old recordings, secret ballots, and a prom that doubles as the Court's coronation, she must choose between the safety of careful silence and the dangerous truth that belonging bought with someone else's exclusion isn't belonging at all. She finds Theo alive, held by fear rather than force, exposes the rigged Court on prom night, and rebuilds the tradition as something the whole town can actually belong to.
about_author: Elodie Ravensworth grew up in a small river town where one annual festival decided everything, an experience that left her permanently suspicious of traditions nobody is allowed to question. She writes young adult stories about sharp-tongued girls who learn that winning an argument and changing a mind are two different victories.

chapters.title: Three Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. We meet her mid-victory: state debate finals won, then a silent, tense dinner where her father's rules go unchallenged, as always. Establishes her double life — flawless in public, erased at home — and her lifeline friendship with Theo, who dares to ask why she never fights back. Emotional beat: the ache of being excellent everywhere except where it matters.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Porch
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Theo misses their weekly playlist swap, then his mother calls in panic. On his porch sit his car keys, neatly placed, phone dead inside. The police call it a runaway; Beatrix knows he'd just been asking questions about the Harvest Court's founder portrait being quietly removed from the library. Emotional beat: dread arriving dressed as ordinary.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with flashbacks to Theo's voice via recovered notes. She finds his hidden notebook: three generations of Delacroix men chairing the Court, and a pattern of families who 'moved away' right after losing the Harvest Queen vote. The deleted playlist, restored track by track, maps to dates and names. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Court of Harrow Bend
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She attends a Court planning meeting undercover as student council liaison and meets Vivienne Delacroix, charming and surgical, who offers Beatrix a place on this year's ballot — an honor her family has never received. The temptation is real: legitimacy, protection, visibility. Emotional beat: power extended like a hand you're afraid to shake.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Theo, revealed alive and hiding at his uncle's cabin outside town, too scared of what the Delacroix network could do to his undocumented aunt to come home. He watches Beatrix get closer to Vivienne and can't tell if she's infiltrating or being absorbed. Emotional beat: trust stretched thin across distance and silence.

chapters.title: Nomination
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Her name appears on the Harvest Court ballot, and her father — for the first time in years — is proud of her. The chapter's cruelty: the validation she's starved for arrives precisely when accepting it means betraying Theo's work. She says yes. Emotional beat: the seduction of finally being seen.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Theo returns secretly; POV splits between the two friends reuniting in the school's sound booth. They find a 1978 recording proving the first Harvest Court was a labor union's inclusion ritual before the Delacroixs bought and rewrote it. But Vivienne anticipated them: the recording disappears, and Beatrix's nomination is publicly questioned over 'rumors about her family.' Emotional beat: the trap closing from both sides.

chapters.title: Careful No More
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Stripped of her nomination and threatened with her father's ultimatum — withdraw or lose the family — she finally argues at home, not to win but to be heard, and discovers her father's compliance was its own long surrender. She chooses exposure over safety and leaks the Court's voter manipulation to the whole school. Emotional beat: identity claimed at last, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Prom Night Coronation
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge at prom, where the Court crowning doubles as the announcement of next year's 'eligibility revisions.' Beatrix takes the stage during the coronation waltz, plays the surviving fragment of the 1978 recording over the gym speakers, and challenges the town to remember what the tradition was for. Students, teachers, and old union families stand up one by one. Emotional beat: the argument she couldn't win alone, won together.

chapters.title: New Tradition
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, weeks later. Vivienne resigns rather than reform; the Court reopens nominations to every family, and Theo comes home openly. Beatrix and Theo start a new playlist — side A for what was lost, side B for what's next — and she runs for student body president on a platform of auditable elections. Her father attends the first open Court meeting, sitting in the back. Emotional beat: belonging that no longer requires anyone's erasure.
